newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Nationalists worth US$3 billion - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Nationalists worth US$3 billion - newspaper.

text.p: Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party, one of the world's wealthiest political parties, had assets worth more than T$85 billion (US$3.09 billion) at the end of 1996, a newspaper reported on Friday.

The Economic Daily News estimated the party's profits from seven holding companies, comprising investments in 121 companies, rose to T$7.5 billion ($273 million) in 1996 from T$7.35 billion ($267 million) in 1995.
The combined capital of the holding companies was more than T$18.5 billion ($673 million), making the party one of the top 15 business conglomerates on the island.
The report did not say how the total assets were calculated. Party officials were not immediately available for comment.
The Nationalists, with 2.6 million members, have ruled Taiwan since they lost a civil war to communist China and fled to the island in 1949.

But their power started to weaken after Taiwan allowed the establishment of new political parties in the late 1980s. The main opposition Democratic Progressive Party has criticised the Nationalist Party's wealth.
Many Nationalist candidates have been found guilty of buying votes in recent years.
